answer: Dishonest graders are slashed and their stake is redistributed, which means a Sybil cluster that tries to vote as a bloc will, on average, lose more from slashing than it gains from manipulating a single verdict. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable.. This holds because each vote is weighted by a track record that only grows through honest participation, turning a Sybil flood into short-lived, low-weight votes.
